description: The brief organizes its inquiry around seasonal learning patterns: comparing how racial and ethnic achievement gaps change across school-year and summer periods to determine when inequality grows.
title: Seasonal learning analysis

description: The article organizes its measurement of speaking around Segalowitz's distinction among cognitive fluency, utterance fluency and perceived fluency.
title: Segalowitz's three notions of L2 fluency framework

description: This framework treats social-emotional learning constructs (academic growth mindset, self-efficacy, self-management) as developmental processes with their own growth trajectories, asking \"whether a student's mean SEL score in 6th grade (status) or growth between 6th through 8th grade is more predict
title: SEL status-and-growth early-warning modeling

description: The study uses a self-controlled before-and-after design where \"the first 6-hour session in the initial semester served as the control condition (conventional teaching), while the subsequent 6-hour session in the following semester served as the experimental condition (debriefing teaching).\" This de
title: Self-controlled before-and-after design with paired measures

description: The review organizes academic self-management interventions for students with emotional and behavioral disorders into five technique types, reporting that \"Self-monitoring interventions were the predominant type of self-management technique used by researchers.\" The taxonomy distinguishes self-evalu
title: Self-management intervention taxonomy for academic outcomes

description: An evaluation paradigm for analytic essay scoring that shifts from normative (inter-learner ranking) to within-learner interpretation of analytic profiles.
title: Self-referential analytic assessment framework

description: An LLM-based agent that labels each discourse sample, then reflects to identify weaknesses in the current coding framework and applies revision actions (modify, add, delete, hold, merge) before labeling the next sample.
title: Self-reflective LLM annotation agent with iterative criteria refinement and short-term memory

description: The article proposes a heuristic for judging when Cronbach's alpha can be read as a reliability index: researchers should examine how semantically similar a test's items are.
title: Semantic similarity heuristic for interpreting Cronbach's alpha

description: A benchmark construction methodology that instantiates prompt privilege on the MedQA benchmark: for each original MedQA question, four additional semantically equivalent prompt variants are generated representing distinct user cohorts — Low Literacy, Everyday User, Educated User, and Prompt Engineer
title: Semantically equivalent prompt-variant benchmark construction for measuring prompt privilege

description: The article proposes a framework that combines artificial neural networks with two typical theoretical diagnostic classification models, the DINA model and the DINO model, within a semi-supervised learning framework.
title: Semi-supervised ANN framework combining ANNs with DINA and DINO diagnostic classification models

description: The article introduces a framework combining semi-supervised learning with deep learning to adjust biased 2PL-IRT parameter estimates caused by nonignorable missingness in VLE data.
title: Semi-supervised deep learning bias-adjustment framework for IRT parameter estimation under nonignorable missingness

description: The article recommends that subgroup measurement decisions in preschool evaluations be deliberate and tested rather than default.
title: Sensitivity analysis for subgroup measurement definitions in education impact evaluations

description: A reusable analytic pipeline in which fixations are filtered (Tobii I-VT), sentence AOIs are classified as topic-introducing, topic-medial or topic-ending, AOI strings are converted to transition matrices, and weighted networks are built in R with igraph to compute strength, betweenness, harmonic ce
title: Sentence-level social network analysis pipeline for eye-tracking reading data

description: The article recommends that future investigations on causal ordering include both marks and test performance as distinct latent variables rather than a single achievement indicator, because single-indicator models yield artificially reciprocal patterns.
title: Separate teacher marks and standardized test performance as distinct latent achievement constructs in longitudinal panel models

description: The article adapts sequence alignment from bioinformatics: group action logs are human-coded into contribution types — \"coordination, monitoring, minor contribution, and major contribution\" — plus a \"gap\" code for more than 24 hours of inactivity.
title: Sequence alignment and clustering for collaborative-learning process analysis

description: This principle recommends administering multiple questions to LLMs sequentially in batches of ten rather than all at once, because the study found batch delivery converged accuracy to 83%–88% with no significant inter-model differences, while simultaneous delivery produced wide dispersion (38%–90%).
title: Sequential batches of ten for LLM multiple-choice evaluation

description: The sequential multiple assignment randomized trial is a design in which \"participants are randomly assigned to intervention components at multiple stages of the intervention,\" with assignments determined by decision rules based on proximal outcomes.
title: Sequential Multiple Assignment Randomized Trial (SMART) design

description: The article argues that teaching happens in series while methodology tests are typically done in parallel, implicitly assuming no interaction effects.
title: Serial testing of instructional combinations

description: The study adapted a coding scheme from Lin et al.
title: Seven-category teacher instructional move coding scheme for collaborative small-group discussions

description: The article organizes feedback design as seven dimensions realizable in the Surveillance testbed: subject (individual vs.
title: Seven-dimension design space of feedback choices for team tutoring testbeds

description: The article develops and applies a comparison framework that identifies characteristics of summative assessments in seven dimensions: cognitive process, transferability, depth of analysis, interdependence, novelty, scaffolding and communication.
title: Seven-dimensional outcome comparison framework for analyzing implicit learning outcomes in summative assessments

description: From a systematic review of 71 studies, the article extracts 22 distinct AI opportunities for medical student assessment and groups them into seven overarching categories called mega-opportunities.
title: Seven mega-opportunities taxonomy of AI in medical student assessment

description: The article identifies \"seven pre-defined outcomes\" for assessing MCQ quality: \"question relevance, question clarity, distractor quality, question accuracy/correctness, item difficulty analysis, and item discrimination analysis (point biserial correlation and item discrimination index)\".
title: Seven-outcome framework for evaluating MCQ quality in health professions education

description: The article proposes a framework of seven epistemological phases for AI-based educational research: \"(1) problem framing, (2) instrumentation and measurement, (3) experimentation and evidence‑based inference, (4) comparisons and replication, (5) building norms and consensus, (6) implementation and i
title: Seven-phase framework for reflecting on how AI methodologies may transform science education research

description: The review adopts the framework of seven primary team learning behaviours: knowledge sharing, constructive conflict, co-construction, boundary crossing, team activity, team reflexivity, and storage and retrieval.
title: Seven primary team learning behaviours framework

description: Applying ANT to classroom talk, the article defines networks of human and non-human actors (texts, boards, instructions) that constitute the socio-material structure of talk.
title: Seven-step recursive ANT analysis of dialogic and non-dialogic classroom talk networks

description: The article adapts ANT into a recursive analytic procedure for classroom talk with seven steps: recognizing actors (human and non-human), tracing connections into assemblages, identifying translations of roles, identifying shifts and changes in the network, delineating interactions' outcomes, examin
title: Seven-step recursive ANT analysis procedure for classroom discourse

description: The article adapts and refines Narciss's content-based feedback taxonomy into seven feedback focus types for annotating written feedback: Task Constraints, Concepts, Elaboration, Clarification, Mistakes, Praise, and Other.
title: Seven-type feedback focus taxonomy adapted from Narciss for written teacher feedback

description: A set of 17 behavioral features distilled from tutor log files and normalized as a percentage of total student actions, designed to \"encompass a wide array of possible help-seeking behaviors\".
title: Seventeen log-derived help-seeking features for assessing help seeking in intelligent tutors
